thread:
matt: Heads-up: invoke-validator-v2 is spiking rejects for tool outputs on route 'qa-assistant' in us-west. Customers seeing tool errors and extra token burn. Console: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/validators :triangular_flag_on_post:

rina: How bad is "spiking"? Any numbers?

matt: Quick tail from metrics:
```
validator.rejects{region=\"us-west\",route=\"qa-assistant\"} = 980 (5m)
fallback.count{route=\"qa-assistant\",variant=\"model-fallback\"} = 905 (5m)
account.tokens_burn{acct=acct-99} = +14% (10m)
```

bao: Can someone run a grouped query on validation_events to see reject_reason distribution and validator commit?
```
SELECT reject_reason, validator_commit, count(*) FROM validation_events WHERE region='us-west' AND route='qa-assistant' AND ts > now()-10m GROUP BY reject_reason, validator_commit ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10;
```

deploy-bot: rollout.change: user=ci-pipeline promoted invoke-validator-v2 region=us-west percent=100 -> 16:05:18 UTC

ana: Wait we thought v2 was staged only. Who promoted to 100%? That was supposed to be gated. :eyes:

ops: Looking at CI logs now. There's an automated promotion that triggers when e2e passes, but the gating rule failed to check the "prod-safe" flag. Filed infra-1602 to add that guard.

rina: Immediate mitigation: revert validator to previous commit or flip route-level gate to "observe" mode so we log rejects but don't hard-stop responses. Which is less risky?

bao: Revert is risky if v1 had a bug. Observe mode (send header + metric) sounds safer. If we can flip only for qa-assistant in us-west, do that.

matt: Command to set observe: `redwoodctl validators set --route qa-assistant --region us-west --mode observe --note "emergency observe after validator-promote"`
deploy-bot: validators.update: route=qa-assistant region=us-west mode=observe requested_by=matt 16:12:03 UTC

ux-lee: UX request: Console should show validator mode inline on the route summary (observe|enforce|permissive) and a one-click sample panel that pulls 50 recent rejects with redaction. Support tickets are flooded.

bao: Telemetry ask: add tags `validator_commit`, `reject_kind` (values: schema_mismatch|enum_invalid|malformed_json), and `fallback_variant`. Also publish `reject_rate` as a ratio metric (rejects/requests) with 1m granularity. Right now it's too noisy to interpret without a denominator.

matt: Also we need a derived billing metric `tokens_spent_on_fallbacks` so billing ops can alert before customers call in.

ops: Alert proposal: page when hard_reject_rate > 0.08 sustained for 3m OR when tokens_spent_on_fallbacks > 5% baseline for 10m. Soft/observe rejects should only increment dashboards, not page.

rina: Small console/UX change: add an audit log entry for any mode flip with actor + diff + reason; make it searchable by route and time. We had a mystery promotion and needed to chase CI logs.

bao: For longer term: implement a soft-fallback policy that returns the tool response but attaches a structured warning in response JSON: `{\"validation\": \"soft_warning\", \"details\": [..]}` and emits a metric. That preserves user experience while keeping signal.

matt: Good. I'll file follow-ups: INF-10123 (ci gating guard), INF-10124 (metrics: reject_ratio & tags), INF-10125 (console: mode + sample + audit). Assign INF-10124 -> bao, INF-10125 -> ux-lee, INF-10123 -> ops.

ops: infra-1602 -> created to add prod-safe flag checks to promotion job. We'll also add an incident note linking these tickets.

ux-lee: I'll prototype the route summary pill and sample drawer today as a feature-flagged change. Low risk.

matt: Thanks. If anyone sees customer-facing errors keep me posted. We'll decide on a post-incident writeup if billing impact > 1 customer. :+1:
